[[File:PC forum, Luke Trust Me errata, 19 January 2012.png|thumb|right|330px|The Players Committee's errata for [[Luke, Trust Me]], posted on its rules forum on 19 January 2012. Six months later the PC's own website card list printed the same sentence with a typo: "Epic Even".<ref name="p676488" />]]
The '''PC Legacy Virtual transcription error history''' is the story of how the [[Players Committee]] (PC) published the text of its [[Virtual Legacy]] cards between 2009 and 2014, and of how that text was copied, and miscopied, from one document to the next. Many Legacy cards have three, four or five versions on this wiki. Most of the extra versions were not new rulings. They were made when a volunteer typed a card into the [[Holotable]] data, when the PC's website card list was generated from that data, and when the PC went back to its own earlier wording in the 2013 Master List or in a card image.

There is an irony at the heart of it. Holotable's card data was never the PC's official text: the PC said the PDFs were official, and the Holotable volunteers themselves refused to change their data until the PDFs changed. Yet when the PC put a full card list on its own website in 2012, that list was built from the Holotable data, typos and all, and for a while it was the most complete text of Virtual Legacy that the PC published.

== The documents ==

Every Legacy card text reached players through some of these documents, in roughly this order.

Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020174512/https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualBlock7_1.pdf Internet Archive]</ref> The PC re-made several sheets later, so some first printings survive only in other copies, or not at all.

== What counted as official ==

The PC was clear about where official text lived. Release sheets were "Official text as of" their date.<ref name="sheet71" /> Its Tournament Guide 2.0 said that rulings and errata "can be found in the 'Current Rulings/Errata' thread" until they were folded into the Advanced Rulebook, and that a new expansion was legal "as defined by the release of the PDF containing the virtual card slips".<ref name="tg20">[https://web.archive.org/web/20160808081200/http://www.starwarsccg.org/Resources/tournaments/Star%20Wars%20CCG%20Tournament%20Guide%202.0.pdf Star Wars CCG Tournament Guide 2.0] (2 December 2013; Wayback, 8 August 2016), § 2.1 and § 2.3</ref> No PC rules document names Holotable, its data or the website card list as a source of card text.

Players held the PC to that. In May 2010 a PC insider, Rogue4, said that the PC's "internal master list" had [[Yoda (V) (Virtual Block 2)|Yoda (V)]] at deploy 4, so the PDFs (deploy 5) were wrong.<ref name="p547489">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=547489#p547489 Re: Have you found Holotable text or image errors?], post by Rogue4 (30 May 2010), Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums</ref> A former World Champion answered: "The master pdf IS the official text. Not some 'internal list.'"<ref name="p547713">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=547713#p547713 Re: Have you found Holotable text or image errors?], post by arebelspy (31 May 2010), Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums</ref> The Holotable volunteer who kept the data, kurtisblow ([[Kurt Schlichting]]), agreed with the player, not the insider: "I'll leave holotable as-is until the PDF's are corrected."<ref name="p547686">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=547686#p547686 Re: Have you found Holotable text or image errors?], post by kurtisblow, signed Kurt Schlichting (31 May 2010), Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums</ref> Asked again in June, he repeated that he would not update it "until the master and vblock2 pdfs are updated".<ref name="p557221">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=557221#p557221 Re: Have you found Holotable text or image errors?], post by kurtisblow (18 June 2010), Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums</ref> JediJer reported on 24 June that the Master List PDF was fixed ("Block 2 pdf will get updated when I get around to it"), and two days later Kurt wrote: "The Yoda (V) correction should be in Holotable now."<ref name="p561177">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=561177#p561177 Re: Have you found Holotable text or image errors?], post by JediJer (24 June 2010), Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums</ref><ref name="p561559">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=561559#p561559 Re: Have you found Holotable text or image errors?], post by kurtisblow (26 June 2010), Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums</ref>

== Holotable: the volunteers' copy ==

Holotable was [[Matt Moseley]]'s program, not a PC product, and its card data was kept by volunteers (the [[Holotable#Card data and its keepers|Holotable article]] credits them by name). For each set they typed the new slips and the errata from the PC's PDFs and forum posts.<ref name="p840511">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=840511#p840511 Re: Have you found Holotable text or image errors?], post by LtPage2 (4 October 2013), Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums: "If you want to fix something, just start from the most-up-to-date CDFs in Holotable and send me the changed file, and I can upload it."</ref> PC news posts spoke of Holotable updates from the outside ("They should be up today from what I've heard").<ref name="news83">[https://web.archive.org/web/20100101222734/http://www.starwarsccg.org:80/news/news.php?id=83 Virtual Set 6.2 is released], post by Rogue4, starwarsccg.org (7 December 2009; Wayback, 1 January 2010)</ref>

Comparing the surviving data files with the dated forum errata shows the same pattern every time: the data followed the PC and never led it.<ref name="r7">Comparison of the Holotable CDF snapshots with the dated forum errata and the 2012 card list: [https://github.com/billbisco/ai-team-skills/blob/main/shared/gemp-legacy-cards/versions/sources/R7-HOLOTABLE-GOVERNANCE.md research notes R7] (11 November 2026), §§ 3&ndash;4.</ref>
* '''It took errata late, or never.''' In 2010 an errata reached the data within days or weeks. From 2011 it took months or years; [[With Thunderous Applause (Virtual Block 5)|With Thunderous Applause]]'s errata of August 2011 never arrived, and most errata posted from November 2013 on are missing from the October 2014 data.<ref name="r7" />
* '''It wrote errata in its own words.''' Volunteers moved sentences ("May not be Disarmed." at the end of [[Darth Vader, More Machine Than Man]] and [[Master Qui-Gon (V) (Virtual Block 5)|Master Qui-Gon (V)]]), wrote out icons as text, and made new typos ("Epic Even", "reshufle", "retireved").<ref name="r7" />
* '''It kept pre-release text.''' In August 2009 JarJarDrinks built "temporary" Holotable files for the new Virtual Block 6 cards from the PC's text spoilers, before the release sheet came out.<ref name="p450850">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=450850#p450850 Re: Temporary Holotable CDFs], post by JarJarDrinks (25 August 2009), Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums</ref> Two of those spoiler texts were never replaced (see [[#Fleet Security Protocols and He's No Jedi|below]]).
* '''It once copied a mistake the PC withdrew.''' On 23 July 2014 the PC posted an errata for AT-RT ([[AT-RT (Errata 4)]]); two days later it apologised for "an error in carrying over some text" and posted the correct wording ([[AT-RT (Errata 5)]]). The 2014 data has the first, withdrawn posting.<ref name="p894811">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=36574&start=40#p894811 Re: Current Rulings/Errata], post by darkjediknight11 (23 July 2014), Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums</ref><ref name="p895797">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=895797#p895797 Re: Current Rulings/Errata], post by darkjediknight11 (25 July 2014), Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums</ref><ref name="r7" />

The data also stamped errata it had taken, as "(Errata Text - September 9th, 2009)" on 143 cards and "June 18th, 2010" on two more; stamping stopped after mid-2010.<ref name="r7" />

== The card list: Holotable goes official ==

[[File:PC forum, sac89837 Errata Listing, 20 July 2010.png|thumb|right|330px|sac89837 ([[Ryan Jellison]]) builds "the Database for the Website" from SW-IP and the Holotable data, 20 July 2010.<ref name="p566763" />]]
The PC website's card database was built by one of the same volunteers. On 20 July 2010 sac89837 ([[Ryan Jellison]]), "putting together the Database for the Website", wrote that he had "exhausted SW-IP and the Holotable.CDF file".<ref name="p566763">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=566763#p566763 Errata Listing], post by sac89837 (20 July 2010), Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums</ref> By February and March 2013 he was still updating the website after fixing the Holotable data.<ref name="p782160">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=782160#p782160 post by sac89837] (February 2013), Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums</ref>

The card lists that the PC website showed from 2012 are, entry for entry, the Holotable data:
* 998 of the 1,058 Virtual Legacy entries captured on 21 July 2012 are identical, character for character, to one of the surviving Holotable files, although no 2011&ndash;12 file survives to compare the rest against.<ref name="r7" />
* Every image link on the card list is the Holotable file path (<code>/starwars/Virtual5-Dark/t_withthunderousapplause</code> becomes <code>images/starwars/Virtual5-Dark/large/withthunderousapplause.gif</code>).<ref name="cl" /><ref name="r7" />
* The card list carries Holotable's own stamps and credits run onto the text, such as "(Immune to Alter.)(Original Concept by …)", and its typos "reshufle" ([[According To My Design (Virtual Block 7)|According To My Design]]) and "retireved" ([[Away Put Your Weapon (V) (Errata 3)|Away Put Your Weapon (V)]]).<ref name="r7" />

So the volunteers' transcription, which the PC never called official and which its own keepers would not change without a PDF, became text that the PC published on its own website. Because the wiki counts every published text as a version (see [[#How this wiki counts versions|below]]), every card-list difference, down to a typo, is a version of its card.

== The Master List goes back ==

The Master List of 27 April 2013 was not taken from the card list. Of 78 Legacy printings where the 2010 Holotable text differs from the sheet and the Master List has a text of its own, the Master List matches the sheet wording in 48 and the Holotable wording in none.<ref name="r7" /> The PC card images usually agree with the Master List. For a card whose card-list text was a Holotable copy of a forum errata, the result is a round trip: forum errata, then card list (the same words with a moved sentence or a typo), then the Master List and card image with the forum's words again.

== PC card images and third wordings ==

Some PC card images print a wording found in no other document. The images can be dated only by outside evidence:
* Three Light Side images, [[Away Put Your Weapon (V) (Errata)|Away Put Your Weapon (V)]], Let's Go Left (V) and Kashyyyk (V), are pixel for pixel the slips in Lee Edwards' V-kit, committed on 9 December 2009, so they were made by then. They are taken to show the September 2009 errata, older than the re-made sheets of December 2009.<ref name="r6">Dating of the PC card images: [https://github.com/billbisco/ai-team-skills/blob/main/shared/gemp-legacy-cards/versions/sources/R6-IMAGE-DATES.md research notes R6] (10&ndash;11 November 2026), with Lee Edwards' [https://github.com/ledwards/swccgvkit-legacy swccgvkit-legacy] (Subversion revision 1, 9 December 2009) and the Wayback directory listings.</ref>
* Most other images are dated only by the server: every file in the Virtual Block 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 and Shields folders carries 25 February 2013; Virtual Block 8, 7 May 2013; Virtual Block 9, 18 February 2014. These are bulk upload dates, and an image may be older than its folder date.<ref name="dirlist" /><ref name="r6" />

== Lost and odd printings ==

* '''The September 2009 sheets.''' The first Legacy printings of Virtual Blocks 1 to 5 (September 2009) were not archived. The sheets that survive were re-made with "official text as of December 7, 2009". For some cards the PC card image is the only record of the earlier wording.<ref name="r6" />
* '''The Virtual Block 7.1 and 7.3 sheets.''' The 7.1 sheet survives only in a copy re-made on 28 July 2010; no copy of the first 7.3 printing (June 2011) survives, so [[Master Kenobi (Virtual Block 7)]] has a reconstructed original.<ref name="sheet71" />
* '''The short Leave Them To Me slip''' and '''the Wookiee Slaving Operation errata post''': see the worked examples below.

== Worked examples ==

Each example shows the documents side by side. Forum screenshots are cropped to the post. Images marked '''CardMaker recreation''' were made for this wiki because no published image shows that text.

=== Luke, Trust Me: "Epic Even" ===

The release sheet of 18 June 2010 begins "Unless your Epic Event on table, deploy on table."<ref name="sheet71" /> On 19 January 2012 the PC changed that to "If you have no Epic Events on table (and did not play an Epic Event at the start of the game), deploy on table".<ref name="p676488">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=48201&start=40#p676488 Re: Current Rulings/Errata], post by Aglets (19 January 2012), Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums</ref> By 21 July 2012 the card list printed the errata with a letter missing: "an Epic '''Even''' at the start of the game".<ref name="cl" /> The 2014 Holotable data has the same typo.<ref name="r7" /> The Master List and the PC card image print the forum's words again.<ref name="ml" />

Versions: [[Luke, Trust Me]] (sheet) → [[Luke, Trust Me (Errata)]] (forum, 2012) → [[Luke, Trust Me (Errata 2)]] (card list, "Epic Even") → [[Luke, Trust Me (Errata 3)]] (PC card image, on the server by 25 February 2013) → [[Luke, Trust Me (Errata 4)]] (Master List, current).

=== With Thunderous Applause: the errata that never arrived ===

The 2009 slip says "At start of your turn, if at Senate" and that the character "loses '''all''' immunity to attrition". The Holotable data of May 2010 reorders the first phrase ("If at Senate, at start of your turn").<ref name="cdf" /> On 26 August 2011 the PC changed "all" to "any".<ref name="p644156">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=48201&start=20#p644156 Re: Current Rulings/Errata], post by Aglets (26 August 2011), Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums</ref> The data never took that errata, so the card list of 2012 still showed the 2010 reorder and "all", a year after the change.<ref name="cl" /><ref name="r7" /> The Master List has the forum text. The PC card image still prints the original text.

=== Leave Them To Me (Death Star II): the short slip ===

The first copy of the Virtual Block 6.1 sheet (official text as of 4 September 2009) gave the shield four sentences.<ref name="sheet61a">Virtual Block 6.1 release sheet, first copy ("official text as of September 4, 2009"), [https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=1375528 forum attachment]</ref> The revised sheet (PDF dated 20 April 2010) printed only the first sentence; its box has room to spare, so the text was not cut for space.<ref name="sheet61b">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualBlock6_1.pdf Virtual Block 6.1 release sheet], revised copy (PDF dated 20 April 2010), slip 23</ref> The two dropped sentences were a penalty ("Your game text at opponent's ◇Swamp and ◇Jungle is canceled") and a benefit ("Your characters present at opponent's ◇Forest are immune to attrition"), so the short card was not simply stronger. No forum or news post announcing a shortening has been found. The Holotable data of May 2010 still had the full text, and the card list ("Subjugated Planet", with a capital P), the Master List, the Virtual Shields sheet of 21 May 2013 and the PC card image all print it in full.<ref name="cdf" /><ref name="ml" /><ref name="vsh">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/vshields.pdf Virtual Shields sheet] (PDF, 21 May 2013)</ref> The short slip may have been a mistake, or the PC may have meant to roll the change back later; it was published either way, and the wiki lists it as a version. The twin printing on Reflections III, [[Leave Them To Me (V)]], never had a short text.

Versions: [[Leave Them To Me (V) (Death Star II)]] (first sheet, full) → [[Leave Them To Me (V) (Death Star II) (Errata)|(Errata)]] (short slip) → [[Leave Them To Me (V) (Death Star II) (Errata 2)|(Errata 2)]] (card list) → [[Leave Them To Me (V) (Death Star II) (Errata 3)|(Errata 3)]] (PC image, on the server by 25 February 2013) → [[Leave Them To Me (V) (Death Star II) (Errata 4)|(Errata 4)]] (Master List, current; the Shields sheet prints the same text).

=== Away Put Your Weapon (V): the image that came first ===

The September 2009 first printing is lost. The PC card image (slip 140E) reads "retrieve up to 5 weapons"; the same image is in Lee Edwards' V-kit of 9 December 2009, and its wording is taken to be the errata of 9 September 2009, the date the Holotable data stamps on that year's errata.<ref name="r6" /><ref name="r7" /> The surviving Virtual Block 2 sheet (official text as of 7 December 2009) spells it "five". The card list has "5" again, plus the Holotable typo "retireved".<ref name="cl" /><ref name="r7" />

Versions: [[Away Put Your Weapon (V) (Errata)]] (PC image, 2009) → [[Away Put Your Weapon (V) (Errata 2)]] (sheet, "five") → [[Away Put Your Weapon (V) (Errata 3)]] (card list, "retireved", current).

=== Deep Hatred (V): a 2006 wording comes back ===

The Virtual Block 4 sheet (official text as of 7 December 2009) says "After the duel (unless it was canceled or tied) Mara is ability = 6". The card list of 2012 says "Unless duel canceled or tied, for remainder of game any Mara is ability = 6", which is the wording of the 2006 Virtual Set 11 card, [[Deep Hatred (V) (Virtual Set 11: Gathering Storm)]].<ref name="cl" /><ref name="r6" /> The PC card image has a third wording with no condition at all ("Mara is ability = 6"); it was on the server by 25 February 2013.<ref name="dirlist" /> The Master List of 27 April 2013 prints the sheet's words again.<ref name="ml" />

Versions: [[Deep Hatred (V)]] (sheet) → [[Deep Hatred (V) (Errata)|(Errata)]] (card list, the 2006 wording) → [[Deep Hatred (V) (Errata 2)|(Errata 2)]] (PC image, no condition) → [[Deep Hatred (V) (Errata 3)|(Errata 3)]] (Master List, the sheet's words, current).

=== Assassin's Blaster Rifle and Anakin Solo: the last upload ===

Both Virtual Block 8.2 cards (sheet of 14 September 2012) have a different text on the card list of 12 December 2012: [[Assassin's Blaster Rifle]] deploys "on an assassin" instead of "on your assassin" and its target "may not be captured" with no "this turn"; [[Anakin Solo]] steals a lightsaber "Once during battle" instead of "Once per turn".<ref name="cl82">PC website card list [https://web.archive.org/web/20121212/http://www.starwarsccg.org/cardlists/VBlock8Type.html VBlock8Type] (Wayback, 12 December 2012)</ref> The Master List of 27 April 2013 prints the sheet words. The PC card images print the card-list words, and the only date for them is the server's: the Virtual Block 8 images carry the server date 7 May 2013, ten days after the Master List.<ref name="dirlist8">Directory listing of the PC Virtual Block 8 image folder ([https://web.archive.org/web/20190818034634/https://starwarsccg.org/cardlists/images/starwars/Virtual8-Dark/large/?C=M;O=A Virtual8-Dark], Wayback, 18 August 2019): every file dated 07-May-2013 13:52.</ref><ref name="r6" /> That is a bulk upload date, and the images may have been made earlier, from the card-list data. The wiki still orders the versions by it, so the card-list wording is current again.

Versions: [[Assassin's Blaster Rifle]] (sheet) → [[Assassin's Blaster Rifle (Errata)|(Errata)]] (card list) → [[Assassin's Blaster Rifle (Errata 2)|(Errata 2)]] (Master List, the sheet words) → [[Assassin's Blaster Rifle (Errata 3)|(Errata 3)]] (PC image, the card-list words, current). [[Anakin Solo]] (sheet) → [[Anakin Solo (Errata)|(Errata)]] (card list) → [[Anakin Solo (Errata 2)|(Errata 2)]] (Master List, the sheet words) → [[Anakin Solo (Errata 3)|(Errata 3)]] (PC image, the card-list words, current).

=== Wookiee Slaving Operation: the struck-through errata ===

On 23 July 2014 the Competitive Balance Team changed the flip condition of [[Wookiee Slaving Operation / Indentured To The Empire]] from two Kashyyyk battlegrounds to two Kashyyyk locations. The forum post shows the change the way an editor marks a draft: "battlegrounds" struck through, "locations" underlined, and the title quoted as "(wookiee Slaving Operation) / [u]Indentured to the Empire[/u]" with its BBCode tag showing.<ref name="p894811" /> The struck and underlined words are not part of the card; the new text reads "locations". The same post carried the [[AT-RT (Errata 4)|AT-RT errata]] that the PC corrected two days later ([[AT-RT (Errata 5)]]).<ref name="p895797" />

Versions: [[Wookiee Slaving Operation / Indentured To The Empire]] (sheet and PC images) → [[Wookiee Slaving Operation / Indentured To The Empire (Errata)]] (July 2014, current).

== How this wiki counts versions ==

The wiki follows rulings made for its card articles in November 2026.<ref name="rulings">[https://github.com/billbisco/ai-team-skills/blob/main/shared/gemp-legacy-cards/RULINGS.md Card version rulings], 8&ndash;11 November 2026.</ref>
* '''Every publication is a version.''' Any text in a document that presents the card (a release sheet, a forum errata announcement, the PC website card list, the Master List or a PC card image) is a version, however small the difference: a typo, a capital or a moved sentence. A document that repeats an earlier text word for word after a different text was published is also its own version, in date order.
* '''Not versions:''' differences forced by the medium (the text card list could not show icons, italics or curly quotes), card text quoted in ordinary forum posts or rules documents, and the Holotable data itself. The Holotable data is used only as evidence of when a wording existed.
* '''Dates.''' A forum errata is dated by its post. A card-list version is dated by the first archive capture of the card list, 21 July 2012, even when the same wording was already in the Holotable data in 2010. A PC card image with no firmer date is placed at its server upload date, and the article says when that date may be later than the image.
* '''Current text.''' The latest version in date order is the current Legacy text, and older versions remain on the wiki with their own pages and images.
